summary.text: HIPS is high-impact polystyrene. Makers sell it for jigs, fixtures, prototypes and light parts with a matt finish, and a printer maker names it for support interfaces. Its HDT at 0.45 MPa is 88 °C. On the H2C it prints at 230⁠–⁠250 °C, and a maker recommends a closed chamber for larger prints.

items.text: high impact strength up to temperatures of -40 ° C
Soluble in many solvents
Bad weather and UV resistance (not suitable for outdoor use)
Finished parts can, for example, ideally be painted with acrylic varnishes.
odorless and tasteless
In the area of 3D printing, the material can be used directly as building material or as support material.
If HIPS is used as support material for overhangs, a second nozzle package is required.
After printing a combination of e.g. ABS and HIPS as support material or PLA and HIPS as support material, the unfinished construct can be placed in D-limonene or orange terpetene solvent.
After a few hours, only the finished part made of ABS, PLA or whatever is left.
The HIPS filament dissolves without residue.
We recommend using HIPS nature, otherwise there may be paint residues on the good part.
The material complies with the requirements for materials intended to come into contact with food.
HIPS may be used for the food and packaging industry.
HIPS may also offer good mechanical properties, such as strength, impact resistance, toughness or heat resistance.
It has great dielectric strength and resistivity.
During printing of HIPS filament small quantities of styrene is released into the atmosphere.
The filament made of HIPS can be used for printing of support parts, but also for functional objects.
Support parts are easily dissolvable in Lemonesol, which doesn’t influence your printed object.
HIPS has good adhesion to other materials and nice surface on the interface.
HIPS has a large shrinkage rate, so you should pay attention to heat preservation when printing, and print in a printer with a closed chamber.

It is a printing material that is completely soluble in limonene, there will be no residue on the surface of the model after dissolution, and the contact surface is smooth and flat; its printing performance is similar to ABS, and can be used for ABS, PETG and other materials to print extremely complex shapes or a supporting material having the shape of a partially enclosed chamber; suitable for multi-nozzle printers.
It is recommended to set the distance between the support and the model to 0, the first contact layer to slow down and turn off the blowing fan to improve the bonding strength with the main material.
It offers similarities to ABS but has high impact resistance making it suitable for printing lower-requirement jigs, fixtures and prototypes at a reduced cost.
FDM® HIPS (high-impact polystyrene) is a low-cost, general-use 3D printing thermoplastic.

items.text: EasyFil HIPS is a versatile high-performance Polystyrene type of 3D printer filament that can be used for 3D printing light and durable parts with a matt surface finish.

Being slightly softer and more flexible than “normal” HIPS filaments - in combination with very limited warping, an excellent thermal stability and flowing behaviour - make EasyFil™ HIPS a truly “easy-to-print” 3D printer filament.
EasyFil™ HIPS is very chemically inert and has outstanding characteristics with respect to hygiene, strength and heat resistance and it prints really smoothly.
EasyFil HIPS is a high-performance and easy to print filament.
It is slightly softer and more flexible than a regular HIPS (High Impact PolyStyrene) filament.
It also has a higher impact resistance than regular HIPS filaments.
EasyFil HIPS is chemically inert and has outstanding characteristics with respect to hygiene.
It has a high strength and heat resistance and it prints really smoothly.
Parts printed with the material are light-weight and can easily be glued together with a variety of adhesives.
High impact resistance
Light-weight and durable
High ESCR resistance
Engineered to meet UL 94HB flame retardancy standards
Easily to glue with various adhesives
Very limited warping
EasyFil™ HIPS printed object will have a really beautiful matt coloured finish.
Fine details and an extremely matte surface finish can be achieved with the material.
Extremely smooth matte surface finish
HIPS styrene glues, epoxy based adhesives, superglues, and contact adhesives
But this material has additional properties to offer like good impact resistance, good dimensional stability, and easy post-processing.
Our HiPS is easy to post process with glue or with sanding paper.
HiPS is a great material to use as a support for ABS because there is a good compatibility between the two materials, and HiPS is an easy breakaway support.
Nanovia PP CF, despite the added cabron fibres, still has a tendency to unstick from the printing surface. By adding a soluble HIPS raft and supports the polypropylene is held in place.

items.text: High Impact Polystyrene (HIPS), as its name indicates, has a very high shock resistance. This resistance also makes it suited as a base 3D printing material, especially for press tools.

items.text: Easy to print

Nanovia HIPS is a soluble support filament that uses a natural citrus based hydrocarbon called Limonene.
It’ close to ABS 3D printing settings makes it ideal for support structures for the latter as well as PA.
Nanovia HIPS can also be used as both a support, and raft material.
Competible with most materials it allows for the easy removal from the 3D printer bed and is soluble in limonene, an extract of essential citrus oils.
Nanovia HIPS used as a support material can be removed manually or dissolved using limonene.

Similar thermal and printing properties to ABS
High impact resistance

When not being used as support material LimoSolve HIPS prints in an extremely bright white colour and has exactly the same characteristics as our EasyFil HIPS filament range.

LimoSolve™ doesn’t contain any added colorants and dissolves completely in Limonene.
This feature in combination with its similar thermal properties to ABS makes LimoSolve™ an outstanding supporting material for complex dual extrusion ABS prints.

This aging shows up both as a gradual change in appearance, i.e. yellowing and loss of surface gloss, and also as a decrease in the mechanical strength.
